punchline: At six David Goggins looked after skates at his father's rink until midnight, and at eight he left with his mother in a car.
thirty_sec: David Goggins grew up working nights at his father's roller rink, with a belt waiting for anyone who stepped out of line. When he was eight, his mother talked his father into a credit card in her name, a neighbor helped, and they drove to Brazil, Indiana. His brother stayed. Life there was poor and hard in new ways: a stutter, hair loss, and teachers who called him stupid.
